teach.goal: Ponte português → inglês com palavras úteis.
solo: Peça uma frase pessoal com 2 das palavras.
group: Palavras: goggles, towel, sunscreen, lifeguard, deep end, swim team.

extra90: Cada aluno escolhe a palavra mais útil e explica por quê.

facts.label: Planos com going to
facts.sub: I’m going to learn to swim. She isn’t going to compete. Are you going to come? Depois de to, use o verbo na forma base.

facts.label: Eu vou
facts.sub: Use am/is/are + going to + verbo para planos: I’m going to learn to swim. She’s going to join a team. O verbo depois de to fica na forma base.

facts.label: Não vou
facts.sub: Para negar, ponha not depois de am/is/are: I’m not going to try the deep end. She isn’t going to swim there yet. Não use don’t com going to.

compare.ask: I’m going to learn to swim.
compare.br: No Brasil, dizemos “vou nadar” com o verbo ir + infinitivo, igual ao inglês.
compare.tip: Diga: “I’m going to learn to swim.”
compare.us: Em inglês, use be + going to + verbo: I’m going to swim. She isn’t going to compete. Are you going to come?

solo: Peça uma experiência pessoal do aluno com essa diferença.
group: Leia as duas colunas e peça que apontem a maior diferença.

extra90: Dupla: um fala como no Brasil, o outro como nos EUA.

pages.title: A public pool · 1/3
paragraphs: It is a hot Saturday morning in Boston. A big public pool is open to everyone. Children laugh and play in the water. Alma sits on a bench near the edge. Her friend Dan arrives with a bag. Alma has an important plan to share.

“Dan, I’m going to learn to swim this summer.” says Alma. “Great plan! Are you going to take lessons here at the pool?” says Dan. “Yes. I’m going to start on Monday, and I’m going to buy goggles.” says Alma.
